name: Buli (Bauchi State)
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists (Cosper 1999, Kraft 1981, Gowers 1907); no grammar or phonology of Buli (Bauchi State) exists.

new_statements.quote: Polci languages have been presented as a genetic sub-unit by Shimizu (1978). This language cluster belongs to Chadic, West A; South-Bauchi West languages, Sub-group North. It comprises the following languages: Zùl, Barang, Dììr, Bili, Nyámzax, Lundur, Pos. From 1995 to 2004, I have done fieldwork on : Dììr, Bili (Buli), Nyámzax (Langas), Pos (Polci) and Luri. Due to difficult conditions of work, the Luri data is very limited; likewise, the Buli data is of very poor quality and will not be used in this work. [...] Po and Za are three-tone languages (Lo = à ; Mid = a; Hi = á) ; the others are two-tone languages (Lo = à ; Hi = a).
new_statements.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2005. Polci Languages. Paper presented at the 3rd Biennial International Colloquium on the Chadic Languages (BICCL 3), CNRS-LLACAN, Villejuif, 24-25 November 2005. HAL halshs-00647754.
new_statements.locator: p.1 of the paper (HAL PDF p.2), introduction, paragraphs 1, 2 and 4

new_statements.rule_in_words: Buli (Bili) is classed, from the author's own 1995-2004 fieldwork, as a two-level (Hi/Lo) tone language like the other Polci-cluster lects except Polci proper (three levels). No statement about word stress or accent is made anywhere; the author explicitly sets his Buli data aside as poor quality.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the only qualification is that Polci proper (Po) and Zaar (Za) have three tone levels whereas Zul, Barang, Diir, Bili (Buli), Nyamzax, Lundur have two.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone levels only; nothing on word- or phrase-level prominence. This is a one-sentence typological remark in a comparative morphology paper, not a phonological description of Buli; the same two-vs-three tone-level remark recurs in Caron 2003 (p.2) and Caron 2006 (fn.3) where Buli is listed but not sampled.
new_statements.identity_note: Caron's 'Bili (Buli)' = Shimizu's Bɨlɨ (no. 15, Polci cluster, SBW sub-group North) = ISO [uly] Ɓuli = Glottolog buli1260 'Buli (Bauchi State)'; the ISO request form itself equates 'Bili (Caron 2005)' with Ɓuli. Not to be confused with Buli of Ghana (Gur, buli1254) or Buli of Halmahera (Austronesian). The ISO form notes two internal varieties (Babban Buli vs Mulan, 53-67% lexical similarity); Caron does not say which village his data came from.

sources.locator: p.1 of the paper (HAL PDF p.2), introduction, paragraphs 1, 2 and 4
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Lists Bili (Buli) among the Polci-cluster languages and states (p.1) that Polci proper and Zaar are three-tone languages while 'the others are two-tone languages'; adds that the author's own Buli field data (1995-2004) is 'of very poor quality and will not be used'.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken; Danladi, Y.; Hon, L.; Aregbesola, A.; Araokanmi, T.; Muniru, J.; Onoja, D. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Some Endangered West Chadic B.3 Languages in South Bauchi State, Nigeria with Notes on Dulubu [dbo]. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-019. SIL International. (via Wayback Machine)
sources.note: Companion survey; mentions Buli only as a former Polci-cluster 'dialect'; its wordlist appendix warns transcriptions are preliminary with 'no in-depth analysis of tones'. Nothing on stress; no Buli data.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2022. Change Request 2022-023 (split of [plj]; create [uly] Buli etc.) and Request for New Language Code Element [uly] Ɓuli (A. Aregbesola, SIL Nigeria).
sources.note: No linguistic content beyond names (Bɨlɨ Shimizu 1978, Bili Caron 2005, Bələ Blench 2020), location (Babban Buli, Sira, Mulan, Nduk), population 2,000, two internal varieties at 53-67% lexical similarity; sources cited: Shimizu 1978, Caron 2005, Blench 2020, Decker & Aregbesola 2022.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2014. Number in South-Bauchi West languages (Chadic, Nigeria). In A. Storch & G. Dimmendaal (eds), Number: Constructions and Semantics. Amsterdam: Benjamins. HAL halshs-00922755 (23 pp.).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Buli appears only as a row of independent pronouns (mí ki ʧi miː kiː wur) and in a plural table.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2013. Loanwords in South-Bauchi-West Chadic Languages (paper + annex, Naples Sept 2012). HAL halshs-00770965 (37 pp.).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Buli (Bu) is one of 14 lects (~1,000 items each in the author's Toolbox database); the only 'Tones' paragraph concerns Hausa loans into Zaar.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2009. Documenting linguistic varieties of the South-Bauchi group. HAL halshs-00647808 (10 pp.).
sources.note: Nothing on stress or on Buli prosody.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2006. South-Bauchi West Pronominal and TAM Systems. HAL halshs-00644372 (18 pp.).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Classification table lists no. 15 Bili (Bùlì) in the Polci cluster; fn.3: 'Zaar and Gùùs (Sigidi) have 3 tone levels; the other languages have 2.' Buli is not in the paper's sample.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2003. South-Bauchi West TAM System. 17th International Congress of Linguists, Prague. HAL halshs-00645356 (14 pp.).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; 'Zaar and Gùùs have three tone levels, the others only two.' Buli listed in classification only.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2002. Review of R. Cosper, Barawa Lexicon: a wordlist of eight South Bauchi (West Chadic) languages (LINCOM Europa 1999). HAL halshs-00644636 (5 pp.).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Reports that Cosper's introduction gives phoneme charts for the eight languages (incl. Buli) and marks two tones throughout; review criticises tone marking for Zaar/Dott only.
